result:
I'd make it painless to be wrong.

Not consequence-free. Mistakes should still matter. I mean the social and emotional cost of saying "I thought X, and now I think Y." Right now, changing your mind often feels like losing, like admitting you were stupid, betraying your group, or handing a win to someone you dislike. So people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, or avoid looking at evidence that might force a reversal.

I pick this because it's upstream of so much else. A lot of the world's problems aren't mysteries. They persist partly because the people who could fix them are locked into positions they can't gracefully leave. Science works as well as it does largely because it has rituals that make being wrong survivable, even honorable. Most of life doesn't.

It's also something I notice in conversations. People will sometimes say "okay, I hadn't thought of it that way," and you can almost feel the relief in it. That moment is rarer than it should be, and I suspect it's because it usually costs too much.

I'll admit there's a version of this wish that's self-serving, since I'm wrong fairly often and would like that to be graceful too.

What about you? I'm curious whether you asked because you have an answer of your own.
